title: XTM 12V/24V Control Box $49.99 (RRP $199.99) + Delivery ($0 C&C/In-Store) @ BCF
body:
Deal: XTM 12V/24V Control Box $49.99 (RRP $199.99) + Delivery ($0 C&C/In-Store) @ BCF

[Buyingcrap] I mean you could use the switches, then if you could find some momentary switches that fit the breaker holes and the usb/12v ports up the top it could be pretty cool. Arcade buttons might work in the socket holes and aliexpress has a wide range of momentary sizes so I'm sure you could get something for the breaker holes. Not a bad idea really.
[Merlict] Thought it was a watch box from the thumb
[locknuts] Anyone know why these have 2 x andersen plug inputs when it's meant to output 50amp max?
[jpanko] What do you mean it's meant to output 50A max ?
[Lingnoi] QUICK CONNECT PLUG 50A total - max. 50A when single use
Connect 2 20amps Anderson's ….
[jpanko] I still don't really understand your question but each anderson plug is protected by a 50A self resetting CB, probably because anderson plugs themselves are rated to 50A. They actually used 6AWG wiring for the anderson plugs which is typically rated to 60-80A.
They're essentially wired in parallel off the same busbar but individually protected.
I'd imagine a pretty typical set up for someone might be:
Anderson plug 1 -> to battery
Anderson plug 2 -> to Solar MPPT -> Solar panel
[Lingnoi] @jpanko: Is he askingwhat happens if U attach 2 X 50a devices through the Anderson's. Total 100a?
[jpanko] @Lingnoi: As long as you've hardwired a fat enough cable (probably 2AWG or 35mm2) onto the busbar with >100A protection you'd be good as gold
[tongme] @Lingnoi: it would work as long as your input cables can handle 100A
[rbimdxe] @jpanko: Just to provide some clarification, SB50 Anderson plugs themselves are rated to 50A for hot disconnections.
For continuous current, they're actually rated at 120A.
Obviously need to use appropriate size cabling and terminals still.
[Lingnoi] @rbimdxe: @jpanko @rbimdxe
Gotcha, this unit itself doesn't have breakers for the Anderson plugs.
[jpanko] @Lingnoi: @Lingnoi Each Anderson plug is protected by a 50A self resetting circuit breaker
[Lingnoi] @jpanko: Hahaha my ADHD only read the line above the info I needed. Thanks bro.
[jpanko] @rbimdxe: Probably shouldn’t be disconnecting anything hot except for an emergency situation…
I didn’t know that about Andersons, my understanding was that there’s a heap of different brands that all make the same shape plugs but obviously aren’t all the same quality or rating. That being said the tech data sheets I’ve seen have only stated 50A as their rating
[jamesorion] @rbimdxe: The plugs themselves might be able to handle it, but the cable they are crimped to won't be rated for anywhere near 120A. Max CSA for a SB50 is only 16mm2.
[jamesorion] Why does your house have 10 x 10 amp sockets on a 16 amp circuit?
[Lingnoi] I don't even have a car and I bought one
[Joshaldinio] What are some good options to use for the switches?
[ozy] LED Electronic rotating disco ball with laser smart lighting switch taped on permanently.
[atlas] Don't have any intention of camping but got one anyway
[A 1] Cheers OP, bought based on your recommendation and the comments here. Though, I have no immediate use for it, as is the OzBargain way.
[gumbs] Sure its cheap, but I don't really understand what people use these for.
My setup has one openable circuit breaker as the main feed/isolator. All the other 7 circuits (which could really be 3 circuits) are switched at the outlet/light.
There's no battery monitor/shunt in this, and no space for extra Anderson plugs tohook it up to the alternator, battery and solar via a dc/DC charger.
[Jackson] Probably that's why it's being cleared out. Decent quality item but with no real appropriate use
[jpanko] I’d be running this straight off the dual battery and will hard wire in anyway (safer long term).
It’s nice having the individual circuits on individual breakers for protection discrimination, that being said in my experience none of my 12v wiring has ever tripped anyway. Probably become more important on a set up after 10+ years of use or if you’re not running your wires through conduit.
I do agree though if it weren’t for the price I wouldn’t buy it I would’ve just bought everything separate and mounted on my own panel but for this price you could barely buy a fuse block!
Shunt should really be mounted at the dual battery as well, not inside one of these boxes.
[muzzy1907] Thanks OP got one for $46.49 using Macq gc
[grimo82] Your paying for the breakers and switching in a neat pack.
The thing itself is next to usless if your devices are self fused or non critical, and have on/off switches ala led camp lights / fridges etc.
Whos using cig plugs and usb-a these days?
[King Tightarse] There are an infinite number of ways wring can go wrong with a camping rig where breakers could help.
Just getting wet is probably the most common
[jpanko] 100W PD usb C charger, Extra camping fridge, Milwaukee battery charger, Starlink, portable power station charger are the main things I use cig for.
USB A comes in handy for me because I have a few devices that only charge off usb A for some reason.
[foxpants] Price now 129.99 :(
Site was showing 49.99 but in cart they'd already corrected it, corrected on site too.
[MrMiser] Dammit! Had it in my cart to buy first thing tomorrow morning.
Should have followed the OzBargain way.. buy first and ask why later 🤣
